newsitem.title: FRANCE: Matif to change futures contract underlying bond.
newsitem.headline: Matif to change futures contract underlying bond.

text.p: The COB stock market regulator said on Wednesday it did not oppose plans by French futures and options exchange MATIF to change the characteristics of the French government bond underlying its futures contract.
The planned changes would apply to contracts starting with the December 1997 bond future contract, the COB said.
The nominal value of the new contract will remain 500,000 francs, but the coupon of the underlying ficticious government bond will be 5.5 percent compared with 10 percent currently.
The maturity of the underlying government bond will be changed to 8.5-10.5 years from seven-10 years.
Options contracts on the bond future will carry the new characteristics beginning with the October 1997 monthly option contract and the December 1997 quarterly option contract, the statement said.
Starting with the December 1997 bond future there must be 40 billion francs outstanding of a government bond issue for it to be eligible for delivery.
